retrieved_documents.title: NameNode, DataNode, and block lifecycle
retrieved_documents.text: The NameNode maintains filesystem metadata and chooses block locations. DataNodes serve block reads and writes and execute creation, deletion, and replication requests. A DataNode receiving or deleting a block can therefore be participating in routine work.

retrieved_documents.text: A file is split into blocks, and each block can be stored in multiple replicas. DataNodes report the blocks they store to the NameNode. Several messages about different replicas of one block are expected and are not evidence of corruption by themselves.

retrieved_documents.title: NameNode, DataNode, and block lifecycle
retrieved_documents.text: The NameNode maintains filesystem metadata and chooses block locations. DataNodes serve block reads and writes and execute creation, deletion, and replication requests. A DataNode receiving or deleting a block can therefore be participating in routine work.

retrieved_documents.title: Replication factor and block reports
retrieved_documents.text: A file is split into blocks, and each block can be stored in multiple replicas. DataNodes report the blocks they store to the NameNode. Several messages about different replicas of one block are expected and are not evidence of corruption by themselves.

retrieved_documents.title: Deletion and freeing storage
retrieved_documents.text: Deletion can cause HDFS to remove blocks or excess replicas as part of normal space reclamation. The fact that a block was removed from one DataNode does not on its own imply unexpected data loss.

retrieved_documents.title: NameNode, DataNode, and block lifecycle
retrieved_documents.text: The NameNode maintains filesystem metadata and chooses block locations. DataNodes serve block reads and writes and execute creation, deletion, and replication requests. A DataNode receiving or deleting a block can therefore be participating in routine work.

retrieved_documents.title: Replication factor and block reports
retrieved_documents.text: A file is split into blocks, and each block can be stored in multiple replicas. DataNodes report the blocks they store to the NameNode. Several messages about different replicas of one block are expected and are not evidence of corruption by themselves.

retrieved_documents.title: Deletion and freeing storage
retrieved_documents.text: Deletion can cause HDFS to remove blocks or excess replicas as part of normal space reclamation. The fact that a block was removed from one DataNode does not on its own imply unexpected data loss.

retrieved_documents.title: NameNode, DataNode, and block lifecycle
retrieved_documents.text: The NameNode maintains filesystem metadata and chooses block locations. DataNodes serve block reads and writes and execute creation, deletion, and replication requests. A DataNode receiving or deleting a block can therefore be participating in routine work.

retrieved_documents.title: Replication factor and block reports
retrieved_documents.text: A file is split into blocks, and each block can be stored in multiple replicas. DataNodes report the blocks they store to the NameNode. Several messages about different replicas of one block are expected and are not evidence of corruption by themselves.

retrieved_documents.title: Deletion and freeing storage
retrieved_documents.text: Deletion can cause HDFS to remove blocks or excess replicas as part of normal space reclamation. The fact that a block was removed from one DataNode does not on its own imply unexpected data loss.

retrieved_documents.title: NameNode, DataNode, and block lifecycle
retrieved_documents.text: The NameNode maintains filesystem metadata and chooses block locations. DataNodes serve block reads and writes and execute creation, deletion, and replication requests. A DataNode receiving or deleting a block can therefore be participating in routine work.

retrieved_documents.title: Replication factor and block reports
retrieved_documents.text: A file is split into blocks, and each block can be stored in multiple replicas. DataNodes report the blocks they store to the NameNode. Several messages about different replicas of one block are expected and are not evidence of corruption by themselves.

retrieved_documents.title: Deletion and freeing storage
retrieved_documents.text: Deletion can cause HDFS to remove blocks or excess replicas as part of normal space reclamation. The fact that a block was removed from one DataNode does not on its own imply unexpected data loss.
